exercises.title: Sum Two Numbers
exercises.description: Write a function that returns the sum of two integers.
exercises.hint: Use the + operator and return the result.

exercises.title: Celsius to Fahrenheit
exercises.description: Convert a temperature from Celsius to Fahrenheit using F = C × 9 / 5 + 32.
exercises.hint: Write 9.0 / 5 instead of 9 / 5, otherwise C++ does integer division and you get 1.

exercises.title: Even or Odd
exercises.description: Return true if n is even and false if it is odd.
exercises.hint: The % operator gives the remainder. What is the remainder when an even number is divided by 2?

exercises.title: Largest of Three
exercises.description: Return the largest of three integers.
exercises.hint: Compare a with b first, then compare the winner with c.

exercises.title: Letter Grade
exercises.description: Return 'A' for 90 and above, 'B' for 80–89, 'C' for 70–79, 'D' for 60–69, and 'F' below 60.
exercises.hint: Check the highest grade first with if / else if, so each later check only runs if the earlier ones failed.

exercises.title: Leap Year
exercises.description: A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except years divisible by 100 are not, unless they are also divisible by 400.
exercises.hint: Check the 400 rule first, then the 100 rule, then the 4 rule.

exercises.title: Sum 1 to N
exercises.description: Return the sum of all integers from 1 to n. If n is 0 or less, return 0.
exercises.hint: Start a total at 0 and add i to it in a for loop from 1 to n.

exercises.title: Count Digits
exercises.description: Return how many digits a non-negative integer has.
exercises.hint: Dividing by 10 removes the last digit. Count how many times you can do that.

exercises.title: Power
exercises.description: Return base raised to the power exp (exp ≥ 0) using a loop, without using pow().
exercises.hint: Start with result = 1 and multiply by base exp times.

exercises.title: Reverse a String
exercises.description: Return a string with its characters in reverse order.
exercises.hint: Loop from the last index (s.size() - 1) down to 0 and build a new string.

exercises.title: Count Vowels
exercises.description: Return how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u, lowercase only) are in the string.
exercises.hint: Loop over each char c in s and check if it is one of the five vowels.

exercises.title: Palindrome Check
exercises.description: Return true if the string reads the same forwards and backwards.
exercises.hint: Compare the first and last characters, then move both ends toward the middle.

exercises.title: Largest Number
exercises.description: Given a non-empty vector of integers, return the largest one.
exercises.hint: Assume nums[0] is the largest, then compare it with every other element.

exercises.title: Average
exercises.description: Return the average of a non-empty vector of integers as a double.
exercises.hint: Add everything up, then divide by nums.size(). Convert to double before dividing.

exercises.title: Count Occurrences
exercises.description: Return how many times target appears in nums.
exercises.hint: A range-based for loop works well: for (int x : nums) { ... }

exercises.title: Factorial
exercises.description: Return the factorial of a non-negative integer. The factorial of 0 is 1.
exercises.hint: factorial(n) = n × factorial(n − 1). The base case is n == 0.

exercises.title: Fibonacci
exercises.description: Return the nth Fibonacci number, where fib(0) = 0 and fib(1) = 1.
exercises.hint: fib(n) = fib(n − 1) + fib(n − 2). You need two base cases.

exercises.title: Sum of Digits
exercises.description: Using recursion, return the sum of the digits of a non-negative integer.
exercises.hint: n % 10 is the last digit and n / 10 is everything else.

exercises.title: Swap with References
exercises.description: Swap the values of a and b. Because they are passed by reference (&), the caller's variables change.
exercises.hint: Use a temporary variable to hold one value while you overwrite it.

exercises.title: Double Through a Pointer
exercises.description: p points to an integer. Double the value it points to.
exercises.hint: *p means "the value p points to". You can read it and assign to it.

exercises.title: Sum an Array
exercises.description: Return the sum of the first size elements of a C-style array.
exercises.hint: arr[i] works on pointers too. It means *(arr + i).

exercises.title: Rectangle Area
exercises.description: Return the area of the rectangle.
exercises.hint: Access struct members with a dot: r.width

exercises.title: Distance Between Points
exercises.description: Return the straight-line distance between two points.
exercises.hint: Distance = sqrt(dx² + dy²). sqrt is in <cmath>.

exercises.title: Counter Class
exercises.description: Finish the Counter class. increment() adds 1, reset() sets it back to 0, and get() returns the current count.
exercises.hint: Each method only needs one line that reads or changes the private member count.
